contacts.institution: Tee's health insurance / her counselor's office
contacts.when: right after the deception was discovered (2007)
contacts.what_was_asked: an appointment with a counselor to cope with the discovery
contacts.what_institution_did: The office said no appointments were available for six weeks and would not pass a message to the counselor.
contacts.quote: I preached out to my health insurance and I said, hey, I'd like to get an appointment with a counselor. And I had seen a counselor previously dealing with, you know, my friend is dying thing, so I made a phone call and they said, oh, well, he doesn't have any appointments for six weeks.
contacts.what_happened_next: Tee wrote a private letter directly to the counselor/doctor.
contacts.notes: A listener psychiatrist read on air in the Q&A attributes such waits to resource shortages.

contacts.institution: Tee's doctor/counselor (whom she had seen before)
contacts.what_institution_did: On reading her letter he called her and saw her within 24 hours; the session helped her.
contacts.quote: I addressed it to his office with attention to him and four days later he got his mail and he opened it and he called me right away, he got me in within 24 hours.
contacts.what_happened_next: "One day, one hour of counseling after the initial trauma was invaluable to me" (@ 9:38).
contacts.notes: This is therapeutic support, not protection from the perpetrator.

contacts.what_was_asked: that the perpetrator not be allowed to keep working as a nurse ('she shouldn't be working on anyone else's children')
contacts.what_institution_did: Asked Tee for a written, mailed account and referred the matter to police, triggering an investigation.
contacts.quote: So what I did was I contacted the California Nursing Board. I told them a lot had happened and they said thank you can you type something up so I did can you mail it to me and I did. And I basically told them what I happened. And the police officer called me and he said, Hey, California nursing board contacted me. It did trigger an investigation
contacts.what_happened_next: Tee never learned whether the license was revoked; five months after discovery the perpetrator wrote that she was working in a PICU, and later reportedly took another job and claimed illness again.
contacts.notes: Outcome of the board's action unknown to the show.

contacts.institution: a police detective (contacted by the nursing board)
contacts.what_institution_did: A detective interviewed Tee for about two hours, took the syringes she had kept to test them, and said 'we will do something'; no result is reported.
contacts.quote: He was a detective. He came here. He sat and he talked to me for probably two hours at the kitchen table.
contacts.what_happened_next: "And he said, but I understand. And we will do something. And I don't know if her license was revoked." (@ 2:03). No charges or result reported.
contacts.notes: He also told her 'don't let this devastate you and move on and just let it go if you can' - presented by Tee as kindly meant.

contacts.when: after the perpetrator's death (December, years later)
contacts.what_institution_did: Tee went to counseling; the season gives no detail of the response.
contacts.quote: So what did I do? First I went to a counselor and then I started working out a lot because that helps clear my head.
contacts.what_happened_next: She also took psychology classes and talked with her professor.

persons.name: Tee
persons.harm: Over almost four years (from about 2002) a coworker at the veterinary hospital where Tee worked faked ovarian cancer, chemotherapy, brain surgery, pregnancies and her son's illnesses, self-inflicting wounds and symptoms. Tee became her main caregiver (meals, moving her five times, bathing her, caring for her children), and was left with lasting trauma, guilt and repeated grief.
persons.perpetrator_role: her coworker and close friend (factitious disorder, as the perpetrator herself later called it)
persons.outcome_quote: And I don't know if her license was revoked. I believe that it was. I do believe that it was. Do I have proof? No, I don't. Do I know for certain? No, but I believe I have to try to believe in the system that that worked.
persons.notes: The deception ended when a neighbor discovered fresh self-inflicted wounds and the perpetrator confessed (s2-e5 @ 7:10), not through any institution. The protection Tee sought (removal from nursing) is not shown to have happened; the perpetrator's own email read on air says she was 'working in the PICU' five months later (s2-e6 @ 4:05), and the neighbor later said she 'went to work someplace else and was saying she was sick again' (s2-e6 @ 18:44). Counseling contacts are coded though they concern coping, not protection. Not coded as contacts: the abortion-clinic nurse who 'looked at me really strangely', the ER that refused to treat the perpetrator ('They knew, but I didn't know'), the psychiatric hold (perpetrator's own treatment, released after 48 hours), and the veterinary hospital itself (the employer was also deceived). Social services contact is coded in the children's records. Evidence: Tee's Nov 14 2007 letter and the perpetrator's emails read on air; Jen, Kurt and Sarah corroborate.

persons.name: [unnamed] perpetrator's son
persons.harm: The perpetrator claimed her young son had seizures (he was on phenobarbital), failing kidneys needing a transplant and a brain tumor; Tee believes she was giving him medications that made him sick (Munchausen by proxy). He was also told for years his mother was dying of cancer.
persons.outcome_quote: However, really strangely, that ex-husband released the child back to her. Really soon? Yes, really soon after. Like, within a month, the child was back at home.
persons.notes: The induced-illness abuse is Tee's belief ('I think she was doing my child's unbi-proxy', s2-e5 @ 12:14), not confirmed by any record; Jen corroborates only the claims (brain tumor, s2-ep2 @ 5:08). Whether any doctor treating him (phenobarbital, kidney work-up) suspected anything is unknown. The father had doubted the seizures (s2-ep2 @ 4:06) but no report by him is mentioned. After the perpetrator's death 'The children were separated. And went to their dad' (s2-e6 @ 16:42) - no institution shown causing that.

persons.name: [unnamed] perpetrator's daughter
persons.harm: Told for years that her mother was dying of ovarian cancer (art-therapy video at 8), took on an adult caregiving role, appeared undernourished, saw her mother's seizures, was turned against Tee, and as a young girl found her mother dead.
persons.outcome_quote: I'm really sorry to inform you, but [perpetrator] passed away last night. The daughter found her. We don't know if it was an overdose intentional or on purpose, but she has passed away.
persons.notes: Her art therapist (arranged by the grandmother) worked with her on her mother's 'cancer' - the deception was not known, so not coded as a contact. Tee: 'You said you were really ill when you were having the seizures in front of your daughter' (2007 letter, s2-e5 @ 25:48). Host: 'emotionally abusing your children' (s2-e7 @ 28:39). The harm ended with the mother's death, not institutional action. The court's return of the child could arguably be read as endangering her; not coded as institutional harm because the story gives no detail.

coder_notes: All three chunk files read in full (120, 115, 8 lines). Season 2 (Something Was Wrong) is a factitious-disorder / faked-cancer deception, not partner abuse; the perpetrator (Tee's coworker) is never named in this file and is replaced by [perpetrator] in quotations. She died of a possible overdose years later; she is not coded as a person harmed. Very little institutional contact: nursing board and a police detective (outcome unknown), social services (did nothing), a custody court (child returned to mother), and Tee's own counseling. Most institutional detail is Tee's account alone. The perpetrator's claims of being abused by her partners are her own and not treated as established. Animals she harmed (e.g. the cat Boomer) are not coded. Earlier contacts with the perpetrator's psychiatric hold, ER and abortion clinic are not coded because the harm to the persons recorded was not raised there. Two unassigned episodes opened; neither discusses this season. My reading was interrupted by a usage limit after s02_02.txt line 115 and resumed from the notes; no file part was skipped.
